nature: exploratory pre-check for future work B (RFM + purchase form); post-hoc relative to D's frozen Test; never replaces any registered result
known_information_before_registration: B's frozen K-means K=3 labels: cluster 0/1/2 = 700/1,263/721 customers; cluster 2 is the high-value group (C2, ~27% of customers, ~75% of Profile sales)
category-level results: RFM groups differ from random groups mainly through C0; C2 does not differ from activity-matched random groups
the hypothesis 'many within-category variant rules come from wholesalers buying only one product' was already refuted with our data
Chen et al. (2012) report ~18 lines per invoice in 2011 and suggest many organisational customers; UCI describes many customers as wholesalers
no quantity, unit-price or order-time distribution of this dataset was inspected for this registration
execution_order: check1 -> check2 -> check3; stop at the first check that fails its rule (later checks are not computed)

data.snapshot: A snapshot 2ae672b7ea6edb7f5e1561b6a64823004dea833e, read through git show
data.lines: data/processed/A_data_preparation/clean_transactions.csv.gz, rows with split == 'profile', is_valid_basket_item == 1 and customer_id in the population; a basket is an invoice_id
data.discovery_baskets: data/processed/A_data_preparation/baskets.csv.gz, split == 'discovery' and is_eligible_for_main_comparison == 1 (the 7,521 baskets used by C and D); check3 only
data.profile_baskets: same file, split == 'profile' and is_eligible_for_main_comparison == 1; only used for the check3 ceiling
data.population: the 2,684 Profile customers of B's frozen labels (data/processed/B_customer_clustering/customer_clusters.csv in the snapshot)
data.taxonomy: data/taxonomy/item_taxonomy_v1.csv (frozen); l2_id, 'other' dropped, one count per category per basket; only used for the check3 target and ceiling
data.no_validation_or_test: no Validation or Test rows are read; the code asserts that every line used has split in {profile} and every basket in {profile, discovery}

check1_bulk_buying_exists.pack_size: pack(i) = most frequent quantity of item i over Profile lines (ties -> smaller quantity), defined only for items with >= 20 Profile lines
check1_bulk_buying_exists.pack_line_primary: line of an item with defined pack(i) >= 2, quantity >= pack(i) and quantity % pack(i) == 0
check1_bulk_buying_exists.pack_line_denominator: all Profile lines of items with defined pack(i) (lines of items with pack(i) == 1 count as non-pack)
check1_bulk_buying_exists.pack_line_generic_descriptive: quantity >= 6 and quantity % 6 == 0 (item-independent version; descriptive only)
check1_bulk_buying_exists.customer_pack_share: share of a customer's lines (in the primary denominator) that are pack lines; customers with >= 5 such lines
descriptives: top 20 quantities with counts and shares
distinct items per basket: quantiles 10/25/50/75/90 and histogram bins 1, 2-5, 6-10, 11-20, 21-50, 51+
share of orders placed Monday-Friday with hour in [9, 17)
tier pricing: for each item x calendar month with >= 10 lines, Spearman rho between quantity and unit_price; report median rho and the share of item-months with rho < 0

pass_rule.P1_1: pack lines >= 30% of the primary denominator
pass_rule.P1_2: share of customers (>= 5 lines) with customer_pack_share >= 0.5 lies in [0.20, 0.80]
pass_rule.decision: continue only if P1_1, P1_2 and P1_3 all hold

check1_bulk_buying_exists.tier_pricing_rule: if median item-month rho <= -0.30, check2/check3 replace the unit-price feature by the relative price unit_price / median unit_price of the same item in the same month; otherwise raw unit price is used

customer_form_features.basket_size: log1p(mean over the customer's Profile baskets of distinct stock codes)
customer_form_features.qty_per_line: log1p(median quantity over the customer's lines)
customer_form_features.pack_share: customer_pack_share from check1 (customers with < 5 primary-denominator lines get the population median)
customer_form_features.unit_price: median unit price (or relative price, see tier_pricing_rule) over the customer's lines, capped at the population 95% quantile and divided by it
customer_form_features.business_hours: share of the customer's Profile baskets placed Monday-Friday with hour in [9, 17)

check2_redundancy_with_rfm.form_type: bulk if pack_share >= 0.5 else scattered (customers with < 5 lines excluded from the cross-tab)
outputs: cross-tab form_type x frozen cluster (counts and row/column shares)
ARI and Cramer's V between form_type and cluster
purity in both directions (Sokol & Holy 2021, eq. 13)
for each of the 5 form features: in-sample OLS R^2 on standardized [R, log1p(F), log1p(M)] (B's feature_matrix)
mean of each form feature by cluster

stop_rule.S2_a: >= 80% of bulk customers are in cluster 2 AND >= 80% of scattered customers are in clusters 0/1
stop_rule.S2_b: R^2 >= 0.60 for each of basket_size, qty_per_line and pack_share
stop_rule.decision: stop if S2_a or S2_b holds

check3_form_predicts_categories.population: population customers with >= 3 eligible Discovery baskets
check3_form_predicts_categories.target: for each l2 category (excluding 'other'), share of the customer's eligible Discovery baskets that contain it

feature_groups.G1_scale: log1p(number of Profile baskets from lines), basket_size
feature_groups.G4_ceiling: G3 + the customer's Profile category profile (same definition as target, on eligible Profile baskets; zeros if none). Uses category content: reference ceiling only

models.ridge: StandardScaler + multi-output Ridge; alpha chosen inside each training fold by RidgeCV over [0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000] (5-fold, mean squared error)
models.random_forest: RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=200, min_samples_leaf=5, max_features=0.5, random_state=0, n_jobs=-1), multi-output

check3_form_predicts_categories.cross_validation: KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=20261122); identical folds for every group and model; predictions clipped to [0, 1]
check3_form_predicts_categories.metric: mean over customers of Bray-Curtis(pred, actual) = sum|p-a| / sum(p+a)
check3_form_predicts_categories.permutation_null: within quintile bins of basket_size, permute the 4 added form features jointly (rows kept together) across customers, then recompute BC_G3 and gap_closed; ridge 200 repeats, random forest 100 repeats; seeds 0..n-1
check3_form_predicts_categories.descriptive_interval: paired customer bootstrap (2000 repeats, seed 20261121) of BC_G2 - BC_G3, per model
check3_form_predicts_categories.pass_rule: for BOTH models: gap_closed >= 0.10 AND gap_closed > 95% quantile of its permutation distribution
check3_form_predicts_categories.decision: if it fails, the formal experiment (plan section 5) is not run

outputs: results/tables/future_B/precheck/ (CSV/JSON) and a results section added to the plan document
